sentences.text:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER Accused in Spl.S.C.No.150/2024 pending before the Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-I, Chikkaballapura, arising out of Crime No.104/2024 registered by Chikkaballapura Women Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 342, 376(2)(n) OF IPC and U/5(l) and 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and under Sections 9, 10, 11 of Prohibition Of Child Marriage Act 2006 is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
2.

entities.text: Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-I, Chikkaballapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for parties.

3. First information report in Crime No.104/2024 was registered by Chikkaballapura Women Police Station against petitioner herein for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 29.07.2024 received NC: 2024:KHC:51389 from the respondent No.2 who is the mother of the victim girl aged about 16 years 4 months.
During the course of investigation in this case, petitioner herein was arrested on 30.07.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation of the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed for the aforesaid offences.
Bail application filed by the petitioner before the Jurisdictional Court in S.C.No.150/2024 was rejected on 30.10.2024.

Therefore, he is before this Court.
4.
Learned counsel for petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition, prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the petition.
6. Learned counsel appearing for respondent submits that he has no objection to allow the petition.

sentences.text: 7. First informant who is the mother of the victim girl had approached the police on 29.07.2024 and has NC: 2024:KHC:51389 submitted a first information wherein, it is averred that her minor daughter, who was studying in PUC, was found crying on 29.07.2024 and on enquiry she informed that about 5 months back, she had met the petitioner herein and thereafter, they started loving each other.
On June, 06th the petitioner had taken her along with him and they had gone to Dharmasthala in a car and on 07.07.2024, they got married at Dharmasthala in the presence of the petitioner's friends.

About 15 days thereafter, petitioner allegedly took the victim girl to Kavery lodge at Chikkaballapura town and in a room in the said lodge, he had sexual intercourse with her inspite of she opposing the same.

It is in this background, first informant had approached police on 29.07.2024.
8.
During the course of investigation, petitioner was arrested on 30.07.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
Ever since then he is in custody.
Investigation of the case is completed and charge sheet is filed.
The statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of Cr.P.C NC: 2024:KHC:51389 was recorded on 08.08.2024.
She has stated that she was in love with the petitioner and she along with the petitioner and his friends had gone to Dharmasthala and petitioner had married her at Dharmasthala.
Subsequently, the petitioner had taken her to a lodge in Chikkaballapur town and had sexual intercourse with her against her wishes.
Thereafter, he once again took her in a car and had sexual intercourse with her.
Then her family members came to know about the same and thereafter, police complaint was lodged.
Petitioner having no other criminal antecedents, who is aged about 24 years is in custody from 30.07.2024.
Investigation of the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
The prosecution in all has cited 41 charge sheet witnesses in the present case.
Trial in the case is yet to commence.
Therefore, chances of the trial being completed in the near future is very remote.
Apprehension of the learned High Court Government Pleader that the petitioner is likely to tamper with the material charge sheet witnesses can be taken care of by imposing appropriate conditions.
NC: 2024:KHC:51389 Continued detention of the petitioner who is an youngster would have an adverse impact on his carrier and future prospectus.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the prayer of the petitioner for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER Criminal Petition is allowed.
